The 2026 Winter 2v2 Tournament is the first OFM event of the year, serving as a community single edition tournament where teams of 2 face each other.

About

Format

  • General Information
    • 2v2 community event
    • Free registration
    • Maximum of 32 teams
    • 25 minutes cap
  • Group Stage - 24th of January, 2026
    • 8 random pools of 3 teams
    • Round-robin format: every team plays every other team twice
    • 6 matches per pool
      • Win = 1 point
      • Loss = 0 points
    • The team with the most points in each pool qualifies for finals
  • Playoff - 25th of January, 2026
    • 8 qualified teams
    • Random single-elimination bracket
    • 8 total matches
    • Losing a match results in immediate elimination
    • A Third Place Match is played between the losers of the Semi-Finals
    • The Final ends in a Bo3
  • Prize Pool
    • Pattern rewards
    • 2 free shop skin of choice
    • One custom OpenFront Masters skin

Chronology
2025 World Cup

The 2026 Openfront World Cup is the biggest tournament of the year 2026, bringing the best of Openfront on a World Cup style format of Trios.

About

Format

  • Group Stage - May 16th & 17th, 2026
    • 4 trio matches played using a match-point system in pools of 4, 6 pools in total
    • Teams earn points based on their maximum land size reached during each match
  • Point Distribution (per match)
      • 1st: 5 points
      • 2nd: 3 points
      • 3rd: 1 point
      • 4th: 0 points


    • Top two teams of each group advance to the 2026 Openfront Spring Major. The 4 best 3rd place teams also advance
  • Scoring Method
    • At the end of each match, referees record the largest territory size each team reached at any moment during the game
    • Teams are ranked using this maximum land value, and points are awarded accordingly
  • Tie-Breaker Rule
    • In case of equal points, they are decided by overall wins or domination over the other team they are tied with.

Prize Pool

  • Unique Pattern – awarded to all teams that advanced the group stage
  • In-Game currency - Caps for group stage, Plutonium for Finals
  • Clan Store - for winning clan
  • Custom Nation Flag - for Finalists
  • The following is awarded to the winners of the event in addition to the previous items:
    • Unique Bomb Pattern
    • Custom 1/1 skins

title: Accounts
html:
An account lets you play OpenFront under a persistent identity. Update 33.0 added account-level usernames, a verified badge and Login with Google.

Usernames and verified badge

  • You can claim an account-level username in the form base.suffix (subscribers can claim a bare name with no suffix).
  • A verified badge is shown next to your account name on player-facing lists.
  • A verified-name toggle lets you choose to play under your account name.

Login with Google

You can sign in with a Google account and link it to an existing account; once linked, the account shows "Linked to Google".

Profiles and stats

  • A shareable player profile shows your game history and includes a Clans tab, and can be linked to directly.
  • The account modal has a Games tab, and stats now live in a dedicated stats modal (previously called "ranking").

See also

  • Clan
  • Update 33.0

title: Ally
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

An ally is a player with whom a temporary alliance has been accepted. Allies can trade, see each other's intent, and cannot normally attack one another directly.

Duration

The standard alliance duration is 5 minutes. A private lobby can set any whole duration from 1 to 15 minutes, or 0 to disable alliances. Thirty seconds before expiry, both players receive an extension prompt; if both accept, the alliance is renewed for the full configured duration.

Requests

An alliance request remains visible for 20 seconds. After sending one, the requester must wait 30 seconds before requesting the same player again.

Breaking an alliance

A player who breaks an alliance becomes a Traitor for 30 seconds unless the partner is already a traitor or disconnected. Nuclear launches can also break alliances under the blast-area rules on the Nuke page.

Trade and embargoes

Allies receive the highest train-stop payout: 35,000 gold to each owner before multipliers. A temporary embargo lasts 5 minutes. “Embargo all” has a 10-second cooldown.

title: Annexation
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Annexation immediately transfers enclosed territory without resolving it tile by tile through a normal attack. Territory changes are reconsidered at intervals slightly over 20 ticks (about 2.1 seconds), offset per player.

Border clusters

The defender's border is divided into clusters using diagonal as well as orthogonal adjacency. A cluster touching an ocean shore or the edge of the map cannot be annexed. Bounding-box checks prevent territory outside the enclosure from being taken.

Largest cluster

The defender's largest border cluster can be annexed only when it touches no unowned tile, is enclosed by one enemy player, and passes the shore, map-edge, and bounding-box safeguards.

Detached clusters

Smaller disconnected clusters can be annexed when enclosed by enemy-owned boundaries and when the same safeguards pass. Several enemy players may surround a detached cluster.

Captor

If an enemy is actively attacking the defender, the enemy with the largest attack receives the annexed land. Otherwise, the enemy owning the largest share of the surrounding border receives it.

Effects

Annexation itself causes no troop loss. Captured buildings change ownership, except Defense Posts, which are destroyed. If the annexation eliminates the player, the normal conquest-gold transfer also runs.

  • Tile
  • Gold

About

The Apex Assembly Cup is a tournament hosted by soothxng and Vlyra, players for Cynosure. It is a versus type tournament where one player or one team will compete individually against another player or team respectively. Tournament organization was aided by Zilka, a member of Cynosure.

Format

  • All teams entered through registration.
  • Stage One
    • Each trios will be divided into single players for the first stage.
    • Every appointed team leader from each trio will be responsible for assigning their teammates to a group of three players, the order of which is determined by randomization.
      • Groups will play a single round-robin format with every win gaining 2 points for the team, with a total of 12 potential points across all players and groups for a team.
  • Stage Two
    • Points from the prior stage will seed now reunited trios seeded into two separate groups based on their points from the prior stage.
      • Groups will play a single round-robin format with every win gaining 4 points, with a total of 16 potential points, plus the points earned from the previous stage.
  • Stage Three
    • The top 4 teams from the prior stage will compete for the top 4 placements in the tournament.
      • First place teams from each group will play each other for the first and second place.
      • Second place teams from each group will play each other for the third and fourth place.

title: Asia
html:
Not to be confused with East Asia.

The inner blast radius is 12 tiles and the outer radius is 30 tiles. Every non-impassable tile in the inner area is destroyed. Each eligible tile in the outer ring has a 50% chance of being destroyed. Destroyed land becomes Fallout; water remains water.

Units inside the 30-tile outer radius are destroyed regardless of the outer-ring tile roll, except for nuclear and SAM missiles in flight. For each destroyed owned tile, the victim loses 5 × current troops / max(1, remaining tiles) from home troops, outgoing attacks, and transports.

Interception

The bomb can be targeted by a SAM Launcher only while it is within a strict 150-tile Euclidean distance of its silo or its target. A reachable SAM interception is deterministic.

Diplomacy

Launching breaks an alliance when the target area contains a partner structure or has more than 100 weighted partner tiles, where an inner tile counts as 1 and an outer-ring tile as 0.5. In team games the launch is blocked if any teammate structure lies inside the outer radius.

title: Attacking Guide
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

This attacking guide explains the shipped v0.33.1 mechanics behind efficient expansion. There is no single best attack percentage: the useful ratio changes with troop growth, borders, terrain, and other players.

Before attacking

Human troop growth per tick is (10 + troops0.73 / 4) × (1 − troops / maximum). Sending troops lowers the home total and may improve growth, but also weakens every defended tile. The default ratio is 20%; T and Y decrease or increase it by the configured increment.

Maximum troops are 2 × (1,000 × land tiles0.6 + 50,000) + 250,000 × completed city levels. A completed city level therefore adds 250,000 capacity, not 25,000.

Choosing terrain

Defended terrainLoss magnitudeWork per tile
Plains8016.5
Highland or desert10020
Mountain12025

Plains are the cheapest and fastest land to take. A Defense Post multiplies those two values by 5 and 3 within 30 tiles. Fallout multiplies both by 5 − 2 × fallout share of land, from nearly 5 toward 3. Overlapping Defense Posts do not stack.

Troop ratio and border

The tile-work budget grows with 5 × attackers / defenders but is clamped, and is also proportional to the shared border plus a small random 0–4 term. A broad border therefore advances faster than a one-tile contact when other factors are equal.

Attacker losses use a blend of the total troop ratio and the defender's troops per tile. Above 100,000 attacker-owned tiles, losses receive the factor (100,000 / tiles)0.35 while speed receives the stronger factor (100,000 / tiles)0.6. Very large empires can become more troop-efficient but slower at converting equal work.

Bots and players

When a human or nation attacks a bot, the terrain-loss magnitude is multiplied by 0.7. Wilderness has its own cheaper formula: attacker loss is terrain magnitude divided by 5 for humans and nations or by 10 for bots. Attacking an active player is usually more expensive and creates an opening for third parties.

Retreating

A retreat order pauses the attack and resolves after 20 ticks (2 seconds). Retreating from another player loses 25% of the survivors; wilderness retreats return all survivors. Opposing attacks cancel troop for troop, so a counterattack can consume both armies quickly.

Conquest and annexation

A player is conquered below 100 remaining tiles. Bots and nations transfer all remaining gold; active humans transfer half, except a human who never attacked transfers none. Enclosed border clusters can be annexed without troop losses when the exact enclosure checks on the Annexation page pass.

Naval attacks

Transport ships are free, carry the selected attack troops at 10 tiles per second, and are limited to 3 at once. A retreat costs 25% of survivors. Warships prioritize transports, so escorting or timing a landing matters on defended seas.

Nuclear attacks

Atom Bombs have 12/30-tile inner/outer radii, Hydrogen Bombs 80/100, and MIRV warheads 12/18. SAM interception is deterministic when a ready missile can reach the trajectory. The MIRV carrier cannot be intercepted, but individual warheads can.

PropertyBot value

title: Buildings
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Buildings are stationary units built on owned land. A placement is valid only when the structure's center is at least 15 tiles from every existing structure. Buildings under construction do not provide their normal effect.

Construction values

BuildingBuild timeGold costUpgradeable
City2 secondsmin(1,000,000, 125,000 × 2owned city levels)Yes
Defense Post5 secondsmin(250,000, 50,000 × (owned posts + 1))No
Factory2 secondsmin(1,000,000, 125,000 × 2owned port and factory levels)Yes
Missile Silo10 seconds1,000,000Yes
Port5 secondsmin(1,000,000, 125,000 × 2owned port and factory levels)Yes
SAM Launcher30 secondsmin(3,000,000, 1,500,000 × (owned launchers + 1))Yes

“Owned levels” includes every completed level, so upgrades advance the same cost sequence as new structures. Ports and factories share one sequence. A player's infinite-gold option makes these costs zero for that player.

Capturing and destruction

When an enemy captures a building's tile, the building changes ownership. A Defense Post is the exception: it is destroyed instead of captured. Nuclear weapons can also destroy buildings inside their blast radius.

title: City
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

A City increases its owner's maximum Troops by 250,000 per completed level. A city takes 2 seconds to build and can be upgraded.

Cost

The cost is min(1,000,000, 125,000 × 2owned city levels). The first four completed levels therefore cost 125,000, 250,000, 500,000, and 1,000,000 gold; every later level also costs 1,000,000.

Troop capacity

For a human player, the normal maximum is:

2 × (1,000 × owned land tiles^0.6 + 50,000) + 250,000 × completed city levels

The city bonus is added after the territory-based term. Bots use one third of the human maximum, while Nations multiply it by 0.5, 0.75, 1, or 1.25 according to difficulty. Infinite troops replaces the human cap with 1,000,000,000.

Capture

A completed city is captured when an enemy takes its tile. Its level and full 250,000-troop bonus per level then belong to the captor.

title: Clan

Not to be confused with Ally or Alliance.

A Clan is a group of players in OpenFront who display a common tag. It is set by putting a tag in your username (for example, “[TAG] Player”).

Members of the same clan are automatically placed on the same team in team-based modes.

Exception

In Free for All (FFA) mode, clan tags do not confer any team affiliation; all participants compete individually, regardless of clan membership.

title: Combat
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Combat converts troops and time into territory. All rates below are the shipped OpenFront v0.33.1 runtime values; one tick is 100 milliseconds.

Ground attacks

Launching an attack immediately moves the selected troops out of the player's home total. Additional clicks on the same target merge into the existing attack. Opposing attacks cancel troop for troop. Humans and nations default to a 20% attack ratio; bots default to 5%.

Terrain values

TerrainBase attacker-loss magnitude MBase work per tile S
Plains8016.5
Highland / desert10020
Mountain12025
Water / impassableNot capturable by ground attackNot capturable

A Defense Post covering the defended tile multiplies M by 5 and S by 3. Overlapping posts do not stack. Fallout multiplies both values by 5 − 2 × (fallout land tiles / total land tiles), which ranges from 5 with very little fallout toward 3 when all land is fallout. When a human or nation attacks a bot, M is multiplied by 0.7.

Player attack formula

Let A be attacking troops, D defender troops, T defender land tiles, and L attacker land tiles. Define:

sigmoid(x, decay, midpoint) = 1 / (1 + e^(−decay × (x − midpoint)))
q = 0.7 + 0.3 × (1 − sigmoid(T, ln(2) / 50000, 150000))
large-loss = L > 100,000 ? (100,000 / L)^0.35 : 1
large-speed = L > 100,000 ? (100,000 / L)^0.6 : 1
traitor-loss = defender is a traitor ? 0.5 : 1
traitor-work = defender is a traitor ? 0.8 : 1

For each captured tile:

current attacker loss =
  clamp(D / A, 0.6, 2) × M × 0.8 × q
  × large-loss × traitor-loss
alternate attacker loss =
  1.3 × (D / T) × (M / 100) × traitor-loss
attacker loss = 0.6 × current loss + 0.4 × alternate loss
defender loss = D / T
work = clamp(D / (5A), 0.2, 1.5) × S × q × large-speed × traitor-work

The attack's tile-work budget per tick is:

clamp((5A / D) × 2, 0.01, 0.5)
× (shared border size + random integer from 0 through 4) × 3

Tiles are captured while the accumulated budget covers their work. The attacker's size therefore reduces both losses and speed above 100,000 land tiles. As the defender's land area grows, q falls toward 0.7, reducing attacker loss and work by as much as 30%.

Wilderness

A wilderness attack receives shared border size × 2 work per tick. Attacker loss per tile is M / 5 for humans and nations or M / 10 for bots. Work per tile is clamp(2,000 × max(10, S) / A, 5, 100).

Retreat and conquest

A retreat order pauses the attack and resolves after 20 ticks (2 seconds). Retreating from a player loses 25% of surviving attackers; retreating from wilderness loses none. A defender is conquered when fewer than 100 tiles remain.

Conquering a bot or nation transfers all of its gold. Conquering an active human transfers half. A human who never launched an attack transfers no gold, preventing starting-gold farming.

Naval and nuclear combat

Transport ships carry ground attacks across water. Warships use hit points and shells rather than the ground formula. Nukes destroy tiles, structures, units, and troops inside fixed blast radii. See the linked pages for their exact values.

See also

  • Terrain
  • Defense Post
  • Warship
  • Nuke

title: Communication
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Communication includes emojis, quick-chat messages, target markers, alliance requests, and embargoes.

Timing

ActionVisible durationCooldown
Emoji to one recipient5 seconds5 seconds per recipient
Quick-chat message3 secondsUses its message action timing
Target marker10 seconds15 seconds
Alliance request20 seconds30 seconds before retrying the same player
Temporary embargo5 minutesEmbargo-all action: 10 seconds

Nation AI often waits until strictly more than 300 ticks—30.1 seconds—before another casual emoji to the same human. Global broadcasts and immediate responses can bypass that longer AI pacing and still use the normal 5-second emoji timing.

Nation relationship effects

Emoji interpretationNation relation change
Easy/friendly emoji+15
Clown−10
Insult−100

Relation values are clamped by the nation diplomacy system. The same emoji can be visual-only between human players.

Targets

A target marker identifies a player or map location for coordination for 10 seconds. It does not itself launch an attack or force AI behavior.

title: Content creators
html:
Just like the links Masterpost, this page's purpose is to list all the OpenFront Content Creators.

There are different kinds or stages of Content Creators within the OpenFront community, each "rank" getting the same perks as the previous one:

  1. Content Creator - They have the Content Creator role in the discord, and immediate image perms (coming with level 3 for other people), they can post in the OpenFront Content channel to promote themselves.
  2. Affiliates - They access the Content Creator channel and can officially cast the different events and tournaments, they also get an all skins access (even though they're obviously not allowed to wear the custom skins, as they're meant to be used by their buyer/customer only)
  3. Partners - Biggest Content Creators, they have a lot of followers and a big community, they also get the opportunity to have their own skin shop

- In order to apply for the Content Creator role, You need 2k views on OpenFront related videos or more than 1000 followers on a streaming site. (multiple video views can be stacked). Once you're eligible, feel free to open a ticket or contact a member of the staff to claim your role !

title: Controls
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

The controls combine keyboard and mouse input. Keyboard actions can be rebound under Settings → Keybinds; the table shows v0.33.1 defaults.

Default keybinds

KeyAction
Space (hold)Alternate terrain/key-point view
MToggle coordinate grid
1 / 2 / 3Build City / Factory / Port under cursor
4 / 5 / 6Build Defense Post / Missile Silo / SAM Launcher under cursor
7 / 8 / 9 / 0Send Warship / Atom Bomb / Hydrogen Bomb / MIRV to cursor
T / YDecrease / increase attack ratio by the configured increment
B / GBoat attack / ground attack at cursor
Shift+RRetaliate against the attacker at cursor
K / LRequest / break alliance with player at cursor
USwap nuclear missile arc direction
Q / EZoom out / in
CCenter camera on the player
W / A / S / DMove camera
Ctrl (Windows/Linux) or left Command (macOS)Build-menu modifier
Left AltEmoji-menu modifier
RReset graphics
FSelect all warships
PPause where local pause is allowed
Period / commaIncrease / decrease game speed where local speed control is allowed

Mouse

  • Left click: select a spawn or attack territory, depending on game phase.
  • Left-drag: pan the camera.
  • Right click: open the build menu; with a boat selected, cancel that selection.
  • Mouse wheel: zoom. Shift+wheel adjusts attack ratio.
  • Alt+left click: open the emoji menu for the selected player.

Mobile

Touch controls expose the same major actions through selection, context, and build-menu buttons; keyboard bindings do not apply.

title: Defense Post
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

A Defense Post strengthens ground defense in a radius of 30 tiles. It takes 5 seconds to build and cannot be upgraded.

Cost

The cost is min(250,000, 50,000 × (owned defense posts + 1)): 50,000, 100,000, 150,000, 200,000, then 250,000 for the fifth and every later post.

Combat effect

For defended tiles inside the 30-tile radius, the terrain loss magnitude is multiplied by 5 and the work required to capture a tile is multiplied by 3. Multiple overlapping posts do not stack. See Combat for the complete loss and capture-speed formulas.

Destruction

Unlike other buildings, a Defense Post is destroyed when an enemy captures its tile rather than changing ownership. Nuclear blasts can also destroy it.

title: Difficulty
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Difficulty changes named Nations. The lobby labels Relaxed, Balanced, Intense, and Impossible correspond internally to Easy, Medium, Hard, and Impossible. Difficulty does not change ordinary Bots.

Resource values

Lobby labelStarting troopsMaximum multiplierGrowth multiplierMain AI intervalSAM quota per city
Relaxed (Easy)12,5000.50.965–99 ticks0.15
Balanced (Medium)18,7500.750.9555–69 ticks0.20
Intense (Hard)25,0001145–59 ticks0.25
Impossible31,2501.251.0530–49 ticks0.30

The interval ranges are inclusive. Nation maximum troops start from the normal human formula and apply the listed multiplier. Troop growth starts from the normal growth formula and applies the growth multiplier.

Diplomacy and AI

Difficulty also changes nation target selection, alliances, betrayal, construction quotas, nuclear behavior, and response timing. A nation's relation penalty when another player attacks it is −60, −70, −80, or −100 from Easy through Impossible.

title: Doomsday Clock
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

The Doomsday Clock penalizes sides that remain below rising territory-control requirements. It has a 600-second, or 10-minute, grace period at every speed.

Thresholds

The six required control shares are 4%, 9%, 16%, 26%, 40%, and 55%. The leading side is exempt. Bots are excluded; humans and named nations are subject to the clock. In team modes, team territory is combined.

SpeedSix ramp durationsPauses after first five stagesFinal threshold reached after game start
Slow292, 292, 292, 292, 292, 290 seconds70 seconds each45 minutes
Normal208, 208, 208, 208, 208, 210 seconds50 seconds each35 minutes
Fast125 seconds each30 seconds each25 minutes
Very fast40 seconds each12 seconds each15 minutes

Penalty

After a side remains below the current bar for 30 seconds, troop drain begins at 2% of maximum troops per second and rises linearly to 5% over the next 90 seconds. Troops cannot be drained below 5% of maximum.

Warship drain begins at 1% of maximum health per second and rises on a steep eighth-power curve to 50% over 90 seconds. Warships stop at 5% health and cannot heal or automatically retreat while their owner is doomed.

title: Factory
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

A Factory is a railroad station and the source of Trains. It takes 2 seconds to build and can be upgraded.

Cost

Factories and Ports share a single cost sequence:

min(1,000,000, 125,000 × 2^(owned factory levels + owned port levels))

The successive combined levels cost 125,000, 250,000, 500,000, and then 1,000,000 each.

Rail station

Every completed factory is a station. A city or port also becomes a station when a factory is within 110 Euclidean tiles. Two stations can connect only when their centers are more than 15 and at most 110 tiles apart, and the computed rail path is shorter than 155.562 tiles.

Train generation

Let F be the owner's total completed factory levels. Once at least 10 ticks (1 second) have passed since that factory's previous train spawn, each of its levels tests once per tick with probability 1 / ((F + 10) × 15). A factory can create at most one train in a tick and needs a reachable city or port station as a destination.

title: Fallout
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Fallout is impassable land left by nuclear destruction. It cannot be owned, crossed by ground attacks, or counted as capturable land for victory thresholds.

Combat modifier

Let f be fallout land tiles and l total land tiles on the map. Every ground-combat terrain loss magnitude and work value is multiplied by:

5 − 2 × (f / l)

The multiplier begins near 5 and declines linearly toward 3 as the map's land becomes fallout. It never reaches 2.5 in the v0.33.1 runtime.

Victory

Fallout is excluded from the denominator used for territorial victory. Free-for-all requires strictly more than 80% of remaining non-fallout land; teams require strictly more than 95%.

See also

  • Nuke
  • Combat
  • Terrain

title: Free for All
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Free for All (FFA) is the standard mode in which each player or named nation competes as an independent side. Temporary alliances are allowed unless disabled in lobby settings, but allies do not share victory.

Victory

The territorial win check runs once per second. A side wins only when it owns strictly more than 80% of all land that is not Fallout. Reaching exactly 80% is not enough.

If the configured match timer expires, the highest-ranked remaining side wins. Regardless of the selected timer, a hard fallback ends a game after 170 minutes.

Diplomacy

The default alliance duration is 5 minutes. Private games may choose 1–15 minutes or disable alliances with 0. Breaking an alliance normally gives the breaker the 30-second Traitor status.

title: Game Settings
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Game Settings are configurable in single-player games and private lobbies. Public matchmaking and ranked modes use their own fixed rotations.

Players and mode

SettingAllowed values
Bots0–400
Named nationsDefault map count, disabled, or 0–400
DifficultyRelaxed, Balanced, Intense, Impossible
ModeFree for All; 2–7 teams; Duos; Trios; Quads; Humans versus Nations
Match timer1–120 minutes
Custom alliance duration0–15 minutes; 0 disables alliances
Private-lobby start delay0–600 seconds; default 3
Player-vs-player spawn immunity0–120 minutes; default 5 minutes when enabled

If spawn immunity is absent from a game configuration, the runtime fallback is 5 seconds. The selected duration prevents human-vs-human ground attacks during that opening period.

Economy

SettingAllowed values
Gold multiplier0.1×–1,000×
Starting gold0.1 million–1,000 million in the UI
Donate goldOn / off
Donate troopsOn / off
Infinite goldOn / off
Infinite troopsOn / off

Host cheats can separately give only the lobby creator infinite gold, a personal gold multiplier, or additional starting gold. The host starting-gold value is added to the normal lobby starting gold.

Map and rules

  • Map: any selectable map.
  • Compact map: uses the manifest's half-width/half-height map data.
  • Random spawn: skips manual spawn selection.
  • Anonymous mode: hides normal player identity presentation.
  • Instant build: removes construction time.
  • Water nukes: nuclear impacts destroy water instead of land.
  • Doomsday Clock: on/off with Slow, Normal, Fast, or Very fast timing.
  • Host cheats: enables creator-only cheat settings.

Units

Each of these can be enabled or disabled: City, Defense Post, Port, Warship, Transport Ship, Missile Silo, SAM Launcher, Atom Bomb, Hydrogen Bomb, MIRV, and Factory.

Availability

Single player omits donation, anonymous-mode, host-cheat, spawn-immunity, and lobby-start-delay controls. Private lobbies include them. Single-player defaults are World, Relaxed difficulty, 400 bots, normal game speed, Free for All, and 2 teams when team mode is selected.

Spawn selection time

ContextSelection phase

Multiplayer with random spawn150 ticks / 15 seconds
Normal multiplayer300 ticks / 30 seconds

title: Gold
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Gold pays for buildings, warships, and nuclear weapons.

Income

OwnerBase income per tickBase income per second
Human player1001,000
Named nation1001,000
Bot50500

The lobby gold multiplier applies to regular income and trade payouts. Host-only cheat settings can instead give the lobby creator a separate multiplier, starting-gold addition, or infinite gold.

Conquest

Conquering a bot or nation transfers all of its remaining gold. Conquering an active human transfers half. A human who never launched an attack transfers no gold, which prevents players from farming unused starting gold.

Donations

Gold donations can be enabled or disabled in private settings. The related troop donation sends one third of current troops and has a 10-second cooldown.

Infinite gold

Infinite gold makes building and unit costs zero for that player. The host-cheat version affects only the lobby creator, while the general private-lobby option applies to human players under that rule.

title: Hydrogen Bomb
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

A Hydrogen Bomb is a large nuclear weapon launched from a completed Missile Silo. It costs 5,000,000 gold and travels 10 tiles per tick.

Blast

The inner blast radius is 80 tiles and the outer radius is 100 tiles. Every non-impassable tile in the inner area is destroyed. Each eligible tile in the outer ring has a 50% chance of being destroyed. Destroyed land becomes Fallout; water remains water.

Units inside the 100-tile outer radius are destroyed regardless of the outer-ring tile roll, except for nuclear and SAM missiles in flight. Troop losses use the same per-destroyed-tile formula as an Atom Bomb.

Interception and priority

The bomb can be targeted by a SAM only while it is within a strict 150-tile Euclidean distance of its silo or target. When a SAM chooses among threats, a Hydrogen Bomb receives a 70,001-point priority bonus.

Diplomacy

Alliance-breaking and teammate-safety checks use the full 100-tile outer radius. A launch breaks an alliance for a partner structure or more than 100 weighted partner tiles; a team launch is blocked if a teammate structure is in range.

title: Links Masterpost
html:
This Masterpost is here as a list of every useful link concerning OpenFront.

Main links : These links are available from the main site.

Discord Server This link leads to the main OpenFront Server, you're probably already in it, that's where most of the information is transmitted and where you can easily contact the staff and ask for help/advices or have suggestions/feedback. Also the place to join if you want to help with the cosmetics, the UI or the UX.

GitHub The link to the game's GitHub main page. As you may already know, OpenFront is an opensource game, meaning that anyone can access the code and submit their contribution to the game, by doing so you access to the Contributor role on the discord server mentionned above along with the Dev discord server. You also gain a free contributor skin that way thus deleting all ads!

OpenFront's Wiki That's where you currently are! The wiki is in constant evolution and may not be perfectly updated, look below to contribute to the wiki by joining the OpenFront Wiki Project.

OpenFront's Reddit That's where you can interact with a smaller part of the community.

Different discord servers related to openfront : Two of these servers are Officials, while the rest is community projects.

OpenFront Dev One of the 2 Official servers, it is for devs, staff, content creators and translators.

OpenFront Masters server The first and only official OpenFront.io tournament organization. By entering this server, you can access the competitive scene and thus the tournaments plannings while also registering for the future tournaments with your clan!

Openfront Hub The OpenFront Hub is a community-driven server built by OpenFront players, for OpenFront players. The goal is to create a central place for community initiatives, shared information, and collaborative projects. Events, initiatives, and the OpenFront Awards 2025 were just the beginning and more things are to come as The Hub grows.

OpenFront Wiki Project server This wiki's server, this is where to go if you need to report an error, ask questions, suggest something, etc...

Openfront Translation server Official Translation Server for OpenFront.io. This is where you can report translation misspellings or add a language. When contributing enough to gain the proofreader role, you also gain a Translator role on the main server and a Translator skin in your inventory, thus deleting all ads!

Affiliate shops : Additional shops for OpenFront content creators, who get a share of the skins bought in their shop.

Ultimus Rex's shop: Rex

Biffeur's shop: Biffeur

FuzeIII's shop: Fuze

EnzoPlays's shop: Enzo

Molky's shop: Molky

UN clan's shop: UN

Other variants and links for the game : These are sometimes used by the content creators for their videos.

https://main.openfront.dev/: One of the devs variants, where the devs try things sometimes.

https://nightly.openfront.dev/: Another dev variant, often used by content creators to test the upcoming updates features.

https://beta.openfront.io/: Where Evan, Lewis and Nebula (admins) host the playtests before launching a new version of the game.

https://trade3.openfront.dev/: This site doesn't have a cap on economy and tradeships (trade and trade2 don't work anymore for cloudflare reasons).

Disclaimer for the two following websites: They should only be used when there's trouble or someone knows what they're doing, it is advised to not use them

https://blue.openfront.io/: One of the two sites used for smooth updates, so the players don't have their game stop in the middle.

https://green.openfront.io/: The other site used for smooth updates.

Other links :

Steam: The OpenFront Steam release is planned for 2026, make sure to have it on your wishlist.

https://openfront-tools.frozenpenguin.media/: Thanks to Flopenguin you can now watch the replay of any game, no matter the version it was played on (as long as you have the game url/game ID of course), it also allows you to test a solo game in any past version.

OFstats: This site lets you see many information and statistics about players, clans and maps. You can keep track of your progress, but keep in mind that the site only takes into account the name of the player, not the player ID, the stats will be wrong if many people use the same name!

Map Making: Here lies information about how to make maps for the game.

Patreon : There is a Patreon were you can subscribe to support the game and get a pretty badge on the discord server!

Atlas: This website allows you to get additional information on maps, such as Nations spawns

Twitch: The Twitch account of Lewis (director), where some community events are hosted, some beta playtests and sometimes tournaments.

Youtube: The official OpenFront Youtube account.

OpenFront Lobbies : A way to know what lobby will appear next.

title: Maps
html:
OpenFront.io contains many interesting and diverse maps which creates a different playing style for each individual map. Some maps are more built for slow expansion, some for quick expansion, some for trade and some for quicker or slower games. A Free for All game is won at strictly more than 80% of non-fallout land; a team game is won at strictly more than 95%. Fallout is excluded from the denominator, and the victory check runs once per second.

Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Version 33 map data

OpenFront v0.33.1 contains 113 selectable maps, excluding four internal tournament layouts. Every current map page lists its exact normal and compact pixel dimensions, land-tile counts, named-nation count, categories, and public-rotation frequency from the shipped manifest. Compact maps use the manifest's map4x data, normally half the width and height of the standard map.

See also the OpenFront Atlas, a community interactive browser of every OpenFront map.

List of Maps

New in Update 33.0

The 22 maps below were added in Update 33.0.

Continental Maps

World

Map of the World (sometimes referred to as the globe or Earth map) is a map that shows all of the 7 major continents of the world as well as all 5 major oceans of the world. This also included islands such as the Caribbean islands, the British isles, Iceland, New Zealand, Madagascar, Japan and others. The map's terrain is comprised of an even amount of flat, hilly and mountainous terrain that is quite evenly spread through the map. However, Asia tends to be more mountainous, Africa tends to be more hilly and South America tends to be more flat. However, it should be noted that most of the map of water and with the Panama and Suez canals being a thing, this results in this being one of the best maps for trade and warships.

Giant World Map

A giant map of the World. The map's terrain is comprised of an even amount of flat, hilly and mountainous terrain that is quite evenly spread through the map. However, Asia tends to be more mountainous, Africa tends to be more hilly and South America tends to be more flat. It should be noted that most of the map is made of water and with the Panama Canal being a thing (the Suez Canal does not exist on the Giant World Map), this results in this being one of the best maps for trade and warships.

North America

Map of Northern and Central America and Greenland. Mostly hilly and mountainous terrain with some plains mostly near oceans and in the northern and eastern parts of the map. There are a lot of water and rivers.

South America

Map of South America, Central America, Florida, and the Caribbean. Mostly flat and mountainous, with some hills mostly in Brazil. Decent amount of water and has the Panama canal, in addition to rivers, making the map good for trade.

Europe

Map consisting of all continental Europe, as well as nearby islands such as: Great Britain, Ireland, Iceland, Corsica, Sardinia and more. It also shows parts of north Africa and a small part of west Asia. The map's Terrain is mostly flat in the eastern and central regions of the map. However, Scandinavia and the Alps are quite mountainous regions, with areas such as Türkiye and Spain being quite hilly and mountainous. It doesn't include Iceland because the map is a bit stretched compared to the old one. However, it should be noted that while nearly all of the map (except the western side) is land, but due to the Mediterranean Sea and Baltic Sea, and rivers, it is quite a great map for ports.

Europe Classic

This map is a duplicate of the older Europe map without rivers. It is not stretched out like the other maps in the game as well. This map has been added because some players’ devices don’t have enough resources to play the new map, and also because the new map excludes Iceland.

Asia

Map of all of continental Asia, as well as it's nearby islands, such as Japan, Indonesia, the Philippines and Sri Lanka. It also shows parts of east Africa as well as eastern Europe. The map's terrain is quite flat in the north, but in the central regions of the map (such as Tibet/west China and Kazakhstan) there are mountains that are difficult to invade through. However, most of the western side of the map is hilly with a few sparse mountains. Areas other than the north that are also flat are: Indonesia, India, east China and south east Asia. However, it should be noted that most of the map is land, but due to long coastlines and islands, building ports is a great strategy.

Africa

Map of the African continent with parts of the Italian peninsula, Middle East, and Mediterranean. Terrain is very hilly and mountainous, making spread slow. Africa also has long rivers allowing for trade farther inland via a port.

Oceania

Map of Oceania and part of South East Asia. This map is mostly water. Mostly plains and hills with some mountains mainly in the northwest. The east of the map is mostly ocean but there are some small islands which makes it good for trade via ports.

Regional Maps

Black Sea

Map of areas surrounding the Black Sea. Mountains everywhere with most of the plains in the northwest and southeast. Center of the map is dominated by water and there are several rivers going across the map. It has the island of Crimea, but most of the map is land. So, it is somewhat harder to attack in the map outside of Crimea. Most of the map is mountain: the flattest part is in the Southern District area of Russia.

Britannia

Map of the British Isles (Great Britain and Ireland) with a segment of northern France (the Pas-de-Calais).

This map also features historic British kingdoms and lordships (making it the one with the coolest flags!).

Gateway to the Atlantic

Map of Spain, France, Gibraltar, and Northwest Africa. It has lots of rivers. The nations there include French and Spanish provinces, as well as ones with names such as "Baguettes", "An anti pope", “Wine”, and “Sardines,” referencing French cuisine and history.

Between Two Seas

Map of the mountainous region between and around the Caspian sea and the Black Sea.

Iceland

Map of the country Iceland. It's mountainous and it has a coastline riddled with fjords and inlets. That makes it not only suitable for land attacks but also for trade.

East Asia

This is a map with a large amounts of water and two large landmasses: Kyushu and the Korean Peninsula. Previously named Japan and Neighbors.

MENA

Map of Middle East and North Africa, with some parts of Southern Europe visible. Mostly hilly terrain with most of the mountains present in the northern part of the map. There are some water and rivers.

Australia

Map of the country Australia. It's especially suitable for land attacks, as the map is one big island and one smaller island named Tasmania.

Faroe Islands

Map of the Faroe Islands, a real life island cluster located in the north Atlantic sea, between Iceland and Great Britain. It is currently under the Kingdom of Denmark. The map itself presents a lot of waterways and it is a good map for naval invasions and trading via ports.

Falkland Islands

Map of the Falkland Islands located outside of Argentina.

It consists of two main islands, surrounded by water on all sides. There are plenty of tiny islands scattered around the main islands.

Baikal

Map of Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia.

It features two sides of the lake, with a large body of water between. In the teams mode this map can tend to become a slow fight fought mostly with nukes as the shore can be well protected with warships.

Halkidiki

A map based on where Greece meets the Aegean Sea in the north.

It features three fingers of land, with plenty of water around it.

Italia

Map of Italy, Sicily, Sardinia, Parts of Balkans, and Parts of the Iberian peninsula. This is great for land attacks, since mostly is just on one land. But when on islands, warships are great for attacking.


Yenisei

A mess of rivers, land, and islands.

Strait of Gibraltar

Not to be confused with Gateway to the Atlantic.

Map of the Strait of Gibraltar.

Two pieces of land separated by the naturally occurring Strait of Gibraltar.


Montreal

A map of a city in Canada home to 1.7 million people. It has some Islands and water.

New York City

This is a map of New York City, home to 8 million people, has 5 peices of land (boroughs) Manhattan, Queens, Bronx, Staten Island, and Brooklyn. Bronx is cut off in this map, but it shows some other parts of Long Island and New Jersey. The most islandous are south of the Long Island. Governors Island is also shown in the middle.

Arcade Maps

As of Update 33.0, arcade maps include More than Luck, Branching Paths and Las Vegas Strip (see New in Update 33.0), and arcade maps now appear in all playlists.

Other Maps

Pangaea

Map of the old continent Pangaea, which already broke apart in real life. It has a few rivers here and there. This map is optimal for land attacks, as there is only one continent, and it is easy to attack other parts of it.

Mars

A map of what Mars might've looked like if it had water on its surface.

Deglaciated Antarctica

This map consists of Antarctica without ice. This leads to the landmass becoming a huge archipelago as the ice no longer connects the landmasses together, making it the map with the most island in the entire game.

Pluto

A map of the planet Pluto if it was converted into water and land. There is a bunch of islands at the north, so it will be great for boat shipping thing whatever.

Unused Maps

This section is dedicated for maps that have previously been available, but no longer are.

It could be related to tournaments, events, or maps that are retired.

Known World

This is a map that has been taken out from the available list of maps to play on. It was previously listed under "Other Maps".

It contained two bodies of land both with surrounding water, based on the book series A Song of Ice and Fire by George R.R. Martin that is also the inspiration for Game of Thrones.

Maps and Images

The height maps are terrain maps. These maps show water as grey-white. The colors are different depending on the terrain, with green for plains, Khaki or Tan for highlands and desert, and white for snow, ice, and mountains. The images can update to remove smaller blue things and add green, white, or Khaki or tan things that got erased by the white.

title: MIRV
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

A MIRV launches one carrier that separates into as many as 350 independently targeted nuclear warheads.

Cost and launch

The cost is 25,000,000 + 15,000,000 × MIRVs previously launched by all players. There is no price cap. A ready Missile Silo is required.

The carrier travels 15 tiles per tick and cannot be intercepted. It separates around the horizontal midpoint of its route, at a vertical coordinate of max(0, target y − 500) + 50.

Target selection

The selected tile is the first destination. Additional destinations must be land owned by the selected enemy when launched, within 1,500 Euclidean tiles of the selected tile, and at least 55 Manhattan tiles from every already chosen destination. The selector makes up to 1,000 outer passes with up to 100 candidates per pass and stops at 350 warheads.

Warheads

Warheads are sent farthest-first. Each waits a random 0–14 ticks, then travels from 22 to 26 tiles per tick: 22 + floor(warhead index / 350 × 5). Individual warheads can be intercepted by SAM launchers.

Each warhead has a 12-tile inner radius and an 18-tile outer radius. All eligible inner tiles and a random 50% of eligible outer-ring tiles are destroyed. Per destroyed tile, the target troop count is 3% of maximum; the excess above that target is reduced by:

500 × (1 − e^(−2 × excess troops / maximum troops))

Diplomacy

Launching a MIRV directly at an ally breaks that alliance. Individual warheads do not run the standard weighted-tile alliance test. MIRV launches are exempt from the standard teammate-structure blast check, although a player cannot select a teammate-owned target tile before the game is over.

See also

  • Nuke
  • SAM Launcher
  • Missile Silo

title: Missile Silo
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

A Missile Silo stores and launches Atom Bombs, Hydrogen Bombs, and MIRVs. Each level costs 1,000,000 gold and takes 10 seconds to build.

Launch slots

Each completed level provides one launch slot. A slot has a 90-tick, or 9-second, cooldown after firing. A newly completed upgrade also starts its new slot on cooldown, so it is not immediately ready.

Launching

When several silos are ready, the game uses the ready silo nearest the selected target. The weapon's own gold cost is paid when the launch is ordered. Atom Bombs cost 750,000, Hydrogen Bombs cost 5,000,000, and MIRVs cost 25,000,000 + 15,000,000 × MIRVs previously launched in the game.

title: Nations
html:
Nations are the other type of bots in an OpenFront match. They can be considered more "complex" or more "human-like". The main difference is that Nations are named after a real-life nation, such as Bulgaria or Estonia. They will use the flag of their nation and spawn near their nation's territory.

Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Difficulty resource values

DifficultyStarting troopsMaximum multiplierGrowth multiplierMain AI intervalSAM quota per city
Easy / Relaxed12,5000.50.965–99 ticks0.15
Medium / Balanced18,7500.750.9555–69 ticks0.20
Hard / Intense25,0001145–59 ticks0.25
Impossible31,2501.251.0530–49 ticks0.30

Intervals are inclusive. Nation gold income is 100 per tick (1,000 per second) before gold multipliers. The selected difficulty does not change ordinary tribe bots.

Information

Nations are commonly encountered adversaries in Openfront. Often considered as the intelligent relatives of the widespread cannon-fodder Bots, they possess characteristics closer to a human player, including the following: Requesting alliances, Constructing Buildings and trading. Another capability in the naval space is sending transports (also known as ships). Nations can also send emojis on special occasions. For example: if you attack a nation, they have a chance to send out clown or angry emojis. Nations can have inaccurate territory in the game. This is either because it is too small to be more than a pixel, or because the borders are too hard to draw. There is a very small chance it gets accurate borders, with high chances of the territory being bigger or smaller on the map.


Combatting Nations

Nations are quite a peculiar entity in OpenFront. Nations are placed second in the purview of intelligence, with bots being last at third and human players placed at first. Nations are quite hard to beat if you aren't sufficiently prepared for them, due to their ability to act closer to humans than bots. It can be very hard to get rid of a nation bot when they commence an attack, but they ineffectively throw their troops at you and significantly reduce their ability to launch a second wave. Use these weaknesses to your advantage and start a noticeable invasion to call other nations around you to help eliminate them. You can also attack when they launch on a player or a fellow nation. If you are prepared, attack a nation after they build infrastructure like ports.

Actions performed by nations

Nations can:

  • Send ships
  • Build (cities, ports, missile silos)
  • Launch nukes
  • Send emojis (mostly angry emojis when you attack them or clown emojis. This means they will fullsend or almost fullsend you (clown) or attack you continuously (angry). You can attempt to ally them to get them off you, and sometimes they accept.)

Trivia

  • Nations can nuke each other, but in multiplayer games, they rarely get the chance since they are often wiped out by the midgame phase.

Alliances

Relations

Numeric relations range from -100 to +100 and map to four named tiers visible on the info screen:

Relationship Value Range Tier
Less than -50 Hostile
-50 to less than 0 Distrustful
0 to less than 50 Neutral
50 or greater Friendly

Any value below Neutral is a hard rejection signal and a value at or above Friendly is a strong accept signal. Relations shift through gameplay events: targeting a nation applies -40, requesting assistance from an ally costs -20 with that ally, nuking applies -100, and various emoji interactions adjust relations in smaller increments.

Sending alliance requests

When a nation's attack logic runs and bordering enemies are present (not when the nation is only expanding into unclaimed territory), the nation considers sending an alliance request to each bordering enemy. The process is a 1/30 roll per enemy per attack pulse, combined with a check that the player type is acceptable (bots only qualify on Easy difficulty), a check that no cooldown or duplicate-request condition blocks the attempt, and a successful evaluation of the alliance decision tree.

The requirements on whether a request can be sent at all requires that alliances are enabled, the target is not the nation itself, the target is connected and alive, the two are not already friendly, no outgoing pending request to the same player exists, and either an incoming request from that player exists (allowing the nation to respond) or the last outgoing request to that player was at least 300 ticks ago.

If a request is sent while the player already has an outgoing request to the nation, the two requests automatically resolve as accepted, 100 relation points are added to both sides (clamped to +100), temporary embargoes are cleared, and in-flight Atom or Hydrogen bombs that would cross the standard weighted-tile or structure alliance threshold are cancelled. MIRV carriers and warheads are not cancelled by this check.

Alliance decision tree

The core decision routine evaluates ten steps in strict order, with the first matching step determining the outcome. The same routine is used both when considering whether to send a request and when responding to an incoming one.

Confusion

A small chance per evaluation that the nation acts erratically. The probability depends on difficulty: 10% on Easy, 5% on Medium, 2.5% on Hard, and never on Impossible. When confused, the nation makes a 50% random accept/reject decision and everything else is skipped.

Traitor partner

If the other player carries the traitor flag, the nation rejects roughly 90% of the time.

Partner has too many alliances

Applies only on Hard and Impossible difficulties. The nation counts non-bot players in the game and rejects if the other player's current alliance count exceeds a threshold: 50% of non-bot players on Hard, or 25% on Impossible.

Threat partner

If the other player is significantly stronger, the nation accepts the alliance as protection if:

  • In Medium difficulty, if the other has more than 2.5 times the nation's troops.
  • In Hard difficulty, if both current troops and maximum troop capacity exceed twice the nation's own.
  • In Impossible difficulty: if any of three conditions hold: troops greater than 1.5x the nation's, or more troops combined with maximum capacity 1.5x higher, or more troops combined with 1.5x the territory.

On Easy difficulty, nations do not recognize threats.

Team games

In team game modes, nations are increasingly unwilling to ally with non-teammates. Rejection probabilities are 25% on Easy, 50% on Medium, 75% on Hard, and 100% on Impossible.

Bad relation

A numeric relation below zero (Hostile or Distrustful) triggers immediate rejection.

Friendly partner

A Friendly relation (value of 50 or higher) triggers acceptance. Harder difficulties introduce a random rejection chance even when the relation is Friendly: Hard accepts 83% of the time when friendly, Impossible accepts 67% of the time.

Nation has too many alliances

The nation checks its own alliance count against difficulty-dependent caps. Easy nations have no cap. Medium nations reject once their alliance count reaches a random value between 4 and 5 (inclusive). On Hard and Impossible, two checks apply: if the nation has at least two bordering non-bot neighbors and the other player is one of them, the nation rejects if accepting would mean nearly all border neighbors become allies. Additionally, Hard caps total alliances at a random 3 or 4, and Impossible caps at a random 2 or 3.

Early game

If still undecided, the nation may accept based on game age. The window and acceptance probability both narrow with difficulty:

Difficulty Window (ticks past spawn) Accept Probability
Easy < 3,000 (~5 minutes) 90%
Medium < 1,800 (~3 minutes) 70%
Hard < 1,800 50%
Impossible < 600 (~1 minute) 30%

Similarly strong

The final fallback compares effective troop pools (current troops plus any troops in outgoing attacks) and tile counts against difficulty-dependent randomized thresholds. The nation accepts if either condition holds:

  • Comparable troops: the other player's total troops exceed the nation's total troops multiplied by a random percentage. The range is 60–69% on Easy, 70–79% on Medium, 75–84% on Hard, and 80–89% on Impossible.
  • Comparable tiles: the other player's tile count exceeds the nation's by a random percentage (70–79% on Easy, 80–89% on Medium, 85–94% on Hard, and 90–99% on Impossible) and the other player's total troops exceed 50% of the nation's

If neither condition holds, the request is rejected.

Betrayal

Before the normal attack target search runs, nations consider whether to betray any of their current allies. The following factors are considered in this exact order, and the first match results in immediate alliance break followed by a forced attack on the former ally.

  1. Weak Ally (Hard and Impossible only): The ally's combined current and outgoing troops fall below 20% of their maximum troop capacity, and the ally has strictly fewer current troops than the nation. This is sometimes called the "MIRVed ally" trigger, since heavy nuke damage often produces these conditions.
  2. Overwhelming Strength: On Easy and Medium, the nation has at least 10 times the ally's troops. Easy nations skip human allies and check only other nations; Medium nations also apply it to humans. Hard and Impossible do not use this trigger.
  3. Traitor Ally (Medium, Hard, and Impossible): The ally currently holds the traitor flag and the ally's troops are below 1.2 times the nation's troops.
  4. Sole Neighbor (Medium, Hard, and Impossible): The nation has exactly one bordering player, that player is the ally, and the ally's troops multiplied by 3 are still less than the nation's troops.

Embargoes and Emojis

On Hard and Impossible difficulty in team games, nations apply embargoes against all non-teammate non-bot players. Outside team mode, embargoes are placed in response to the relationship status Hostile. Embargoes are lifted when relationships reach 0 or higher (Neutral) on Easy/Medium, 50 or higher (Friendly) on Hard, and embargoes will never auto-lift in Impossible.

When a neighbor places an embargo on the nation, the nation applies a one-time -20 relation penalty. Removing the embargo reverses this penalty.

Insult emojis received from a player apply -100 relation and trigger a response emoji. Peace emojis on Easy difficulty grant +15 relation and may produce a love reply.

Construction

The construction system runs on every nation's main AI tick and twice more between main ticks (at one-third and two-thirds of the attack rate interval). Each call attempts at most one meaningful action (either placing or upgrading a single structure) with defense posts handled on a separate fast path that does not count against normal pacing limits.

Decision branches

When a construction call begins, the AI first checks whether a defense post is needed in response to a land invasion. If the nation has already placed at least one normal structure and is under sufficient attack, this branch fires; if it determines a post is needed but cannot place one, the entire economy build for that call is skipped. Otherwise, the AI checks two pacing gates: a cooldown specific to nations that began the game with high gold, and an off-phase window used in team games to let nuke spending proceed without interference. If neither gate blocks, the AI proceeds to the main structure logic.

The main structure logic considers a few special-case openers, then iterates through ports, factories, SAM launchers, and missile silos in that order, building the first one whose quota is unmet. If no structure was built during this loop, a city attempt follows.

Defense posts

When a nation is under land attack and has already placed at least one structure, the system may change to building defense posts before considering any economic construction. The threshold that triggers this is an attacking troop count of at least 35% of the nation's own troops. Defense posts are an emergency response separate from the economic build order. They are never the first structure a nation places, and boat invasions do not trigger them, only land attacks.

Nation Difficulty Action in Land Attack
Easy Will never construct a defense post when under attack.
Medium 50% chance per call, 1 post maximum near the front.
Hard/Impossible Number of posts scales with attack, up to ⌈ Ratio of incoming troops 0.4 ⌉ {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left\lceil {\frac {\text{Ratio of incoming troops}}{0.4}}\right\rceil }} (ie. 80% incoming troops leads to 2 maximum posts)

The front is defined as tiles on the nation's border that touch an attacker's territory. Candidate placement tiles are sampled from up to 25 tiles in a depth ring between 0.75 and 1.5 times the standard border spacing, where border spacing equals the outer blast radius of an atom bomb. If the nation's territory is too small for this ring, the requirement is relaxed and falls back to random territory samples.

If the defense threshold is met but placement fails such as no valid tiles or insufficient gold, the system blocks all other structure-building for that tick.

Pacing Events

High starting gold

The following only applies to nations with at least 3 million starting gold. On Hard and Impossible difficulty, if nukes, silos, and SAM launchers are all enabled in the lobby, the first structure such a nation builds is a SAM launcher rather than economic infrastructure. This is intended to spread SAM coverage before structures cluster within a single nuclear blast radius.

After the opener, these nations apply a cooldown between successive placements. The first two structures incur no wait; the third requires 250 ticks (about 25 seconds) after the previous placement; the fourth requires 150 ticks; and the fifth and beyond require 100 ticks each.

Post save-up

In team games with missile silos enabled, once a nation's gold reaches its save-up target, construction enters an oscillating pattern of 15 seconds on and 15 seconds off (150 ticks each). The oscillation is synchronized with the nuke AI.

City scaling and quotas

Nation construction quotas are mainly derived from city count. When cities are enabled in the lobby, the AI uses the actual number of cities owned. When cities are disabled, it substitutes a rough estimate based on territory, computed as

max ( 1 , ⌊ Tiles Owned 2000 ⌋ ) {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \max {(1,\left\lfloor {\frac {\text{Tiles Owned}}{2000}}\right\rfloor )}}}

The target count for each structure type is ⌊ Cities × r ⌋ {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \lfloor {\text{Cities}}\times r\rfloor }} , where r is a type-specific ratio:

Structure Ratio per city Notes
Port 0.75 Requires costal access.
Factory 0.75 Multiplies by 0.33 if costal and ports are enabled.
SAM Launcher 0.15 to 0.30 Scales with difficulty.
Missile Silo 0.20 First silo has a 0.40 ratio. Hard cap of 3 silos.
City No quota; always attempted as a fallback once other quotas are fulfilled.

The SAM ratio increases with difficulty: 0.15 on Easy, 0.20 on Medium, 0.25 on Hard, and 0.30 on Impossible. Cities are handled specially. They are not part of the quota-driven loop and have no upper limit other than gold availability and the perceived-cost mechanism. After the loop runs, if no other structure was built, the AI always attempts a city placement, provided cities are enabled.

Any structure type disabled in the lobby is skipped.

Perceived cost

Construction is linked to nuclear weapon saving through a perceived-cost mechanism that inflates the apparent price of structures until the nation has banked enough gold for its preferred nuclear load out.

Lobby Setup Target Gold
Missile Silos Disabled The cost of 1x SAM
Team Mode The cost of 1x Hydrogen Bomb
MIRV-enabled (FFA style) The cost of 1x MIRV + 1x Hydrogen
Hydrogen Bombs Only The cost of 5x Hydrogen Bombs
Atom Bombs Only The cost of 20x Atom Bombs
No Nukes The cost of 1x SAM

While the nation's gold is below their target, the perceived cost of a structure is Perceived Cost = ⌈ Real Cost × ( 1 + k ⋅ n ) ⌉ {\displaystyle {\displaystyle {\text{Perceived Cost}}=\lceil {\text{Real Cost}}\times (1+k\cdot n)\rceil }} where n {\displaystyle {\displaystyle n}} is the number of that structure type already owned and k {\displaystyle {\displaystyle k}} is a type-specific inflation rate:

  • Most structures use k = 1 {\displaystyle {\displaystyle k=1}} meaning each existing city effectively doubles the marginal cost of building another.
  • SAM launchers use k = 0.3 {\displaystyle {\displaystyle k=0.3}} .

Once gold reaches the save-up target, perceived cost equals real cost, and the nation can build at normal prices. After a large purchase depletes the bank, inflation returns.

Building and upgrading

When a nation's total structure count divided by tiles owned exceeds approximately one per 1,500 tiles the AI considers upgrading an existing structure of the target type rather than building a new one, provided the type supports upgrades. If at least one upgradable structure of that type exists, the AI selects an upgrade target.

On Easy, a random eligible structure is chosen 70% of the time, versus on Hard and Impossible, the AI scores candidates by SAM coverage weighted by SAM level and picks the best, with a 50% chance of selecting the second or third best instead. Upgrade percentages vary with difficulty: roughly 70%/40%/25%/10% from Easy to Impossible reflect how often randomness overrides scoring.

If structures of the target type exist but all are currently upgrading, the AI waits rather than building new ones, except when zero of that type exist.

Tile selection

The AI samples up to 25 candidate tiles, evaluates each against type-specific scoring criteria, and selects the highest-scoring tile that passes the standard build validity check.

For ports, candidates are random shore tiles on water that shares an ocean or lake component with at least one other player; isolated water bodies do not qualify, since ports there cannot generate trade. As of Update 33.0, the AI also avoids placing ports on lakes with fewer than 3,000 water tiles in the full-size map. For all other structures, candidates are random owned tiles within the territory's bounding box, with up to 100 attempts per sample to find a valid owned tile.

Scoring uses two distance constants derived from nuclear configuration: the border spacing equals the outer atom bomb blast radius, and the structure spacing is twice that value. These caps prevent scoring from continuing to reward distance indefinitely.

Structure Type Scoring Summary
Missile Silo + City
  • Terrain magnitude, rewarding higher ground.
  • Distance from the border up to the border spacing cap.
  • Distance from another same-type structure up to the same-type structure cap.
  • City only: Distance from factories.
Ports
  • Distance from other ports (encourages spread).
Factory
  • Terrain magnitude, rewarding higher ground.
  • Distance from the border up to the border spacing cap.
  • Distance from another same-type structure up to the same-type structure cap.
  • Distance from cities.
  • Costal nations build fewer factories due to 0.33 ratio.
SAM Launcher
  • Terrain magnitude, rewarding higher ground.
  • Distance from the border up to the border spacing cap.
  • Distance from another same-type structure up to the same-type structure cap.
  • Medium and above: Bonus scoring for every city, factory, port or silo within SAM range.
  • Hard/Impossible: 25% chance that AI shifts to covering under-protected structures, weighing by w ( 1 + Existing Coverage ) {\displaystyle {\displaystyle {\frac {w}{(1+{\text{Existing Coverage}})}}}}

Rail Connectivity

On harder difficulties, factory and city placement also considers the rail network. The chance that connectivity scoring applies on a given call depends on difficulty: never on Easy, roughly 60% on Medium, roughly 75% on Hard, and always on Impossible.

When active, the AI builds a list of reachable train stations once per call. Each station is weighted by its source: the nation's own city, port, or factory stations receive a weight equivalent to the ratio of self-trade gold to ally-trade gold, approximately 0.29. Stations belonging to allies weigh 1.0; stations belonging to teammates or other tradeable players weigh 25/35 (about 0.7143). Bot stations and embargoed players are excluded.

For a candidate tile, the AI looks at stations within the train range, which is more than 15 and at most 110 Euclidean tiles away, groups them by cluster, and takes the maximum weight in range from each cluster. Isolated stations contribute their weight individually. The sum is multiplied by the structure spacing constant and added to the tile's existing score.

When a map has more than one nation per 7,500 land tiles, a nation's first port or factory is prioritized before the normal quota loop. The effect is that nations on harder difficulties place factories and cities to connect into profitable rail networks, particularly favoring proximity to ally infrastructure, rather than placing them on terrain considerations alone.

title: Nuke
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Nukes are missiles launched from Missile Silos. OpenFront v0.33.1 has three nuclear weapons.

WeaponCostSpeedInner radiusOuter radius
Atom Bomb750,00010 tiles/tick1230
Hydrogen Bomb5,000,00010 tiles/tick80100
MIRV warhead25,000,000 + 15,000,000 per earlier global launch22–26 tiles/tick (carrier: 15)1218

Blast resolution

All non-impassable tiles in the inner radius are destroyed. Each eligible tile in the outer ring has a 50% chance of destruction. Destroyed land becomes Fallout. Units inside the outer radius are destroyed even if their outer-ring tile survives, except nuclear and SAM missiles in flight.

With water nukes enabled, impacts destroy water instead of land. The irregular boundary is generated from 16 angular samples with random radii between the inner and outer squared radii, followed by one 60%/20%/20% smoothing pass. Impassable tiles are never destroyed.

Troop damage

Atom and Hydrogen blasts apply a loss for each destroyed owned tile: 5 × current troops / max(1, remaining tiles). This is applied to the victim's home troops, outgoing attacks, and transports. MIRV warheads instead reduce excess troops above 3% of maximum using their own nonlinear formula.

SAM interception

Atom Bombs, Hydrogen Bombs, and MIRV warheads are targetable only while within a strict 150-tile Euclidean distance of their source or destination. A SAM Launcher fires only when its 12-tiles-per-tick missile can reach the trajectory in time. The MIRV carrier cannot be intercepted.

Diplomatic effects

A standard nuke breaks an alliance if the target area contains a partner structure or more than 100 weighted partner tiles; inner tiles weigh 1 and outer-ring tiles weigh 0.5. Team launches are blocked when a teammate structure is in the outer radius. MIRV uses its separate direct-target rules.

title: OpenFront.io

headings.text: Openfront Masters and Eigen Labs tournament

html:
OpenFront.io is a real time strategy game with simple controls. It can be played online against other players and bots, or just against bots.

The game software itself is open source, the source code can be found on Github under openfrontio/OpenFrontIO.

Strategy

Winning in OpenFront.io is achieved by efficiently conquering land while deterring attackers. The victory condition is domination (80% of total land). The defeat condition is elimination (0% land). The map is divided into lands and waters. Naval gameplay is about controlling trade ship routes to buy cities, defenses, and nukes (which are used to disrupt a snowballing player). Trade ships automatically path between ports, and warships can be used to capture trade ships. Land gameplay is about controlling lands to snowball your army and steamroll other players. Lands have elevation, which affects the base cost to capture the land. Mountains are more costly and take longer to capture than grasslands.

HI

OpenFront Masters (OFM) has been announced to be the official, primary tournament platform for OpenFront. This is currently ran and managed by IAmLewis, the Openfront masters director and the community manager who has been a part of the project for over 9 months.

Openfront Masters and Eigen Labs tournament

On the 18th of October, Iamlewis announced the partnership and first event in the new series of events. It remains to see what these are going to be like an the impact that Iamlewis can have on this new competition partnership

title: Port
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

A Port is a shore building used by trade ships and warships. It takes 5 seconds to build and can be upgraded.

Cost

Ports and Factories share a single cost sequence:

min(1,000,000, 125,000 × 2^(owned port levels + owned factory levels))

Trade ships

Each port level attempts to create a Trade Ship once per second. Attempts become less likely as global trade-ship traffic grows and more likely after that port's failed rolls. The exact probability is documented on the Trade Ship page. A destination must belong to another player who can trade with the owner and must be connected through water.

Warship support

Warships are created at the nearest owned port. Each port level provides one repair dock and contributes 5 hit points per tick to a shared active-repair pool, split among its docked warships. Docking requires a range of 5 tiles. Separately, any owned port within 150 Euclidean tiles gives a warship passive healing of 1 hit point per tick.

Rail station

A port becomes a railroad station when a completed factory is within 110 Euclidean tiles. Train trade at a port follows the same payouts as a city station.

Capture

A port and all of its completed levels are captured when an enemy takes its tile. Trade ships and warships then recalculate their valid routes and port ownership.

title: Railroad
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Railroads connect stations and carry Trains between players' cities and ports. Rails are generated automatically; they are not purchased separately.

Stations

  • Every completed Factory is a station.
  • A completed City or Port becomes a station when a factory is within 110 Euclidean tiles.
  • Factories are routing waypoints. Only city and port stops pay gold.

Connections

Station centers must be more than 15 and at most 110 Euclidean tiles apart. The generated rail route must also be shorter than 110 × 1.4142, or 155.562 tiles. Routes may traverse intermediate factory stations.

Train generation

With F completed factory levels in total, each factory level rolls once per tick with probability 1 / ((F + 10) × 15) after at least 10 ticks have passed since that factory's previous spawn. The roll is made only when the factory has an eligible destination cluster, and each factory creates no more than one train per tick.

title: Teams
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Teams groups players and nations into sides that share a victory condition. Lobby formats include 2 through 7 teams, Duos, Trios, Quads, and Humans versus Nations.

Victory

The game checks once per second. A team wins only when its combined territory is strictly more than 95% of all non-fallout land. Exactly 95% is not enough. When a match timer expires, the highest-ranked team wins; a 170-minute hard fallback also applies.

Team rules

Teammates cannot normally attack each other's land. Standard nuclear launches are blocked when a teammate structure is within the weapon's outer blast radius. MIRV is exempt from that structure-area check, but a living teammate's tile cannot be selected as the direct target.

Teammates can trade for a 25,000 base train payout to each applicable owner. Lobby settings may enable gold and troop donations.

Doomsday

When the Doomsday Clock is enabled, a team's land is combined for the threshold and the leading team is exempt.
