title: Trade
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Trade creates gold through sea routes and rail routes. Embargoes and relationship rules determine whether two players can trade.

Trade ships

Ports attempt trade-ship generation once per second for each level. Generation has no hard ship cap; its exact adaptive probability is on the Trade Ship page. For a completed water-route length d, each owner receives:

floor((75,000 / (1 + e^(−0.03 × (d − 300))) + 50 × d) × gold multiplier)

A warship may capture a trade ship after its initial 2-second shore immunity. The captured ship pays only the captor when it reaches the captor's nearest active reachable port.

Train trade

Station relationshipBase payout to each applicable owner
Allies35,000
Teammates or other tradeable players25,000
Same owner10,000 to the train owner

Only city and port stops pay gold; factories are routing waypoints. After the first 10 stops, a train loses 5,000 of base payout per additional stop, with a 5,000 floor. The gold multiplier applies.

Embargoes

A temporary embargo lasts 5 minutes and prevents new trade between the affected players. “Embargo all” has a 10-second cooldown.

See also

  • Port
  • Train
  • Railroad

title: Trade Ship
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

A Trade Ship is an automatic one-way trip between two players' Ports. On arrival, both owners receive the same gold payout. The ship has 1 hit point and travels 1 tile per tick, or 10 tiles per second.

Generation

Every 10 ticks (1 second), each completed port level rolls once. For a port with r consecutive rejected rolls and s trade ships currently in the game, its denominator is:

D = floor((100 / (r + 1)) / (1 − sigmoid(s, ln(2) / 50, 400)))
spawn probability per level = 1 / D

Each failed level roll raises that port's rejection count by 1; a spawn resets it to 0. There is no hard global trade-ship cap. With no rejections, example denominators at 0, 100, 200, 300, 350, 400, 450, and 500 global ships are 100, 101, 106, 125, 149, 200, 299, and 500.

Destination

The destination must be another player's reachable port, connected through water, with trade allowed between the players. A candidate's base weight is its port level. Three independent bonuses each add another port level of weight: route distance of at least 300 tiles; being among the nearest clamp(number of candidates / 3, 4, number of candidates) candidates; and having a friendly owner.

Payout

For actual route length d, both owners receive:

floor((75,000 / (1 + e^(−0.03 × (d − 300))) + 50 × d) × gold multiplier)

If a warship captures the ship, it returns to the nearest active reachable port of the captor; only the captor receives the payout. If no such port exists, the captured ship is deleted.

Capture

A trade ship is safe from piracy for 20 ticks (2 seconds) after leaving shore. A warship captures it within a Manhattan distance of 5, pursues at 2 tiles per tick, requires an active reachable home port, and will not hunt beyond its 100-tile patrol radius.

title: Train
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

A Train travels automatically through connected railroad stations. It moves 2 tiles per tick, or 20 tiles per second, and is drawn with five carriages between its head and tail engines.

Generation

Let F be the owner's total completed Factory levels. Once at least 10 ticks have passed since that factory's previous train spawn, each of its levels rolls once per tick with probability 1 / ((F + 10) × 15). The factory must have a reachable city or port destination and creates at most one train per tick.

Route

A train chooses uniformly among eligible city and port stations. Factories can be intermediate waypoints but do not pay gold. Stations must connect through segments whose centers are more than 15 and at most 110 Euclidean tiles apart, with each computed rail path shorter than 155.562 tiles.

Payout

Allied players35,00035,000
Teammates or other tradeable players25,00025,000
Same owner10,000—

The global or player gold multiplier applies. After the train's first 10 trade stops, each additional stop reduces its base payout by 5,000, to a floor of 5,000.

title: Traitor
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

A Traitor is a player temporarily marked for breaking an alliance. The status lasts 30 seconds.

How it is applied

Breaking an alliance marks the breaker unless the former partner is already a traitor or is disconnected. Nuclear alliance breaks follow the same diplomatic system.

Combat effect

The penalty applies while the traitor is defending. Anyone attacking the traitor multiplies attacker loss per captured tile by 0.5 and work per tile by 0.8. At the same work budget, that 0.8 factor permits about 25% more tile progress; it is not a 20% slowdown to the traitor's own attacks.

Nation behavior

Named nations are much more likely to reject an alliance request from a traitor and may betray an allied traitor depending on difficulty and troop strength.

title: Transport Ship
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

A Transport Ship carries an army over water and starts a ground attack on landing. It is free, has 1 hit point, and travels 1 tile per tick, or 10 tiles per second.

Launching

A player can have at most 3 transport ships at once. The normal attack ratio is 20%, and no port is required. If no path exists, the launch is cancelled and the troops are returned.

Landing and retreat

On reaching its target, the transport creates a ground attack with its surviving troops. Retreating returns the ship toward owned land and removes 25% of the surviving troops. If the destination is destroyed by a nuke, the ship automatically retreats. When no retreat destination is available, its troops are returned directly.

Combat

Transport ships are the highest-priority normal target for enemy warships. They have no veterancy or repair behavior and are destroyed by one successful hit.

See also

  • Combat
  • Controls

title: Tribes
html:
Tribes are the named bot factions that fill out public games (see Bots). Update 33.0 added custom tribe names, letting players buy a tribe name that can appear on bot tribes in public games.

Custom tribe names

  • Custom tribe names are bought and managed from the new Tribes tab in the store.
  • A purchased tribe name can appear on bot tribes in public games.
  • Boosts, also bought in the store, make your tribe appear more often; the store shows when your next boost expires.
  • A public tribe-name leaderboard tracks how tribes are doing, including their active boost counts.

Tribe name themes

Update 33.0 also added a tribe name themes system for maps. Real-world maps ship with themed tribe names, and mappers can define custom tribes — including custom tribe spawn coordinates — in a map's info.json.

title: Troops
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Troops defend territory and are committed to ground attacks and transport ships. OpenFront advances 10 ticks per second.

Starting troops

Player typeStarting troops
Human25,000
Human with infinite troops1,000,000
Bot10,000
Nation — Relaxed / Easy12,500
Nation — Balanced / Medium18,750
Nation — Intense / Hard25,000
Nation — Impossible31,250

Maximum troops

For a normal human player with t owned land tiles and c completed city levels:

maximum = 2 × (1,000 × t^0.6 + 50,000) + 250,000 × c

Bots use one third of that maximum. Nations multiply the human result by 0.5, 0.75, 1, or 1.25 on Easy, Medium, Hard, or Impossible. Infinite troops sets the human maximum to 1,000,000,000.

Growth

For current troops x and maximum m, base growth per tick is:

(10 + x^0.73 / 4) × (1 − x / m)

Bots multiply this by 0.5. Nations multiply it by 0.9, 0.95, 1, or 1.05 by difficulty. Growth becomes zero at maximum and can be negative if the player is above the current maximum.

Attacks and donations

The default ground and naval attack ratio for humans and nations is 20%; a bot's default land ratio is 5%. Troops committed to an attack leave the home total immediately. A normal troop donation sends one third of the sender's current troops and has a 10-second cooldown.

Nuclear damage

Atom and Hydrogen blasts reduce home troops, outgoing attacks, and transports for every destroyed tile. MIRV warheads instead drive the target toward 3% of maximum troops. Exact formulas are on the Nuke page.

title: Unofficial Projects
html:
Unofficial community projects utilize Openfront data or interact with the Openfront systems.

The Openfront Api provides endpoints to query game, player, and clan data: you can list game metadata within a two-day window, fetch full game details, and retrieve player info and session lists by player ID; clan endpoints include a top-100 leaderboard (weighted wins with a 30-day half-life) and detailed clan stats and sessions over optional time ranges

For Software and Tools related to maps, see Map Making.

Note that some of these projects may be work in progress, incomplete, or abandoned.

Web Apps

OpenFront Atlas

An interactive atlas and browser of OpenFront's maps — continental and regional — with thumbnails and per-map details.

  • openfront-atlas.xyz

OpenFront.io Replay Analyzer

A Web Application to analyze OF games

  • ofra.vimacs.workers.dev
  • Author: scamiv
  • Version: v28

FrontPlus.io

FrontPlus.io is a companion web platform for OpenFront.io players.

  • https://frontplus.io/

Software

All software linked below is community-created and not official in any capacity. Use at your own risk. Always review any code you download before running it.

OpenfrontIO Api Client (JS/TS)

An unofficial, robust JavaScript/TypeScript client for the OpenFront API.

Academic Research project for a sophisticated deep reinforcement learning system for training AI agents to play OpenFront.io.

Tools related to automating/cheating, gameplay modification, or forks of the Official OpenfrontIO game are not to be included here. Inactive software/tools will be flagged as inactive when they cease to function. If you verify software working on a more recent version than listed here, please contribute an update!

title: Update 15.0
html:
Update 15.0, previously named 0.15.0, deployed on the 16th of February 2025, was a big update that took 6 weeks of development.

New Features

  • Implemented flags.
  • Implemented Creative mode. (later changed to options in the single player menu)
  • Toggles for bots & nations for single player and private lobbies.
  • Enabled click on URL to join lobby.
  • Multiple UI & quality of life improvements.
  • Replaced pngs with svgs for better looking icons.
  • Overhaul and redesign for the front page.
  • Allow non-hosts to see players in private lobby.
  • New OpenFront logo.
  • Added MIRV (Multiple Independent Reentry Vehicle) nuclear weapon.
  • Added construction time for buildings (to prevent spamming defense posts when getting attacked)
  • Added 5-second grace period at game start to prevent spawn killing.
  • Added keyboard shortcuts: WASD for movement, shortcuts for zoom.
  • Implemented new win condition system - conquer 80% of non-irradiated land to win.
  • Added tick counter.
  • Combined battleship & destroyer into new "warship" class.
  • Improved leader board to show non-fallout percentage land owned.
  • Almost full UI rewrite to support mobile.
  • Humans now have distinct color palette.
  • Allow brackets in names for alliance tags.
  • Names checked for offensive content.
  • Public games now use random maps.

Performance Improvements

  • Reduced memory footprint by by over 10x (1gb => 60mb).
  • Reduced main thread CPU usage by over 70%.
  • moved all game logic into a background thread for smoother gameplay.
  • now playable on mid-low end smartphones.

Fixes

Variety of bug fixes.

See also

  • Update 16.0

title: Update 16.0

  • A PWA (Progressive Web App) has been implemented.

  • A new map has been added: Mars. It is only accessible in private lobbies or single player games, the map won't be selected for public games.

  • Toggles for hiding/showing UI elements, emojis and terrain have been added.

title: Update 21.0
html:
Update 21.0, previously named Update 0.21.0, was released on the 6th of April 2025, added various new features, most notably the Team mode, Multilingual support and multiple new maps.

New Features

Team Mode

Red vs. Blue team, a team wins if they occupy more than 80% of the terrain. There is also a gray bot team. Members in the same clan (with [CLAN] in front of their name) will always be placed in the same team.

Gameplay

  • Players can now donate gold.
  • A game option to disable nukes has been added.
  • Missile silos now have a cooldown.

New Maps

  • Between Two Seas
  • Japan and Neighbors
  • Known World
  • Australia
  • Iceland

Revised Maps

  • North America
    • Slightly smaller size
    • Improved river and lake systems
    • Mississippi now connects to northern lakes with 3+ exits to the sea
  • Africa
    • Slightly smaller size
    • Improved river and lake systems
    • Great Rift Valley lake system now linked with Congo basin and rivers to the south
    • Main river network has 3 exits to the sea
  • Europe
    • Rivers and lakes implemented across the continent
    • The entire North African coast is now included (full Mediterranean)
    • Iceland has been removed
    • Additional nation bots
    • Improved coastline details
  • MENA
    • Nile, Tigris and Euphrates rivers implemented
    • Improved coastline details
    • The map bounds have been extended further west and restricted slightly in the north
  • South America
    • Amazon river basin implemented, connected to the Orinoco basin with 2 exits to the sea
    • Rio de la Plata basin implemented
    • Added coastline details
    • Added the map to the rotation

Flags

  • 43 new flags
  • Improvements to 9 existing flags

Multilingual Support

Translations for the game's starting menu have been added for these languages:

Combat & Military

  • Nukes now properly reduce attacking troops and transport ships, consistent with their effect on other population. (#350)
  • SAM launchers now avoid targeting the same nuke twice, improving their defensive capability. (#270)
  • The warship shell lifetime has been increased to 2 seconds after the death of the warship that shot the shell, preventing unfair advantages when a ship backs away while fighting. (#354)

Trade & Economy

  • Trading with allied ports and nearby ports is now prioritized:
    • 2x more likely to trade with ports belonging to an ally OR those close by.
    • 3x more likely to trade with ports that are both allied AND close by. (#335)
  • Trade embargoes are now automatically created when the player is attacked by other players, adding strategic consequences to aggression. (#353)

Performance Improvements

  • Fixed a bug causing nations to spawn too frequently.
  • Various other performance enhancements.

title: Update 22.0
html:
Update 22.0, previously named 0.22.0 was released on the 25. of April 2025. It increased the team count, made various meta changes and some QoL changes, along with bugfixes and other small improvements.

New Features

Team mode

  • Players with the same clan tag will now be sorted into the same team.
  • There can now be up to 7 teams in public games.

Gameplay

  • Nations will now attack structures with Atom Bombs.
  • SAM launchers now protect against MIRVs.
  • There is now a multitabbing detection.

Naval & Combat

  • Defense posts now launch weapons similar to warships, but at a lower frequency.
  • When trying to attack a nation that can only be reached through a transport ship, a transport ship will automatically be sent.

Maps

  • A new map has been added: [Faroe Islands]
  • Maps are now categorized

Customization

  • Translations have been updated
  • Some flags have been updated
  • The user settings have been added to the main menu.

languages

• Arabic

Note: This is still in Beta of making this section.

Bug fixes & Performance improvements

  • Transport ships will now spawn at better locations.
  • Buildings can no longer be stacked.
  • Warships no longer target trade ships within rivers.
  • Warships no longer pirate trade ships destined for allied ports.
  • Unit rendering has been improved to be more efficient.
  • The radial menu can now be closed with right click.
  • Screen bounds & transform calculations are fixed.
  • An option to anonymise names has been added.
  • Enhanced the visual clarity of key inputs in the instructions.
  • The radial menu and the player info panel will also update live instead of needing to be re-opened to update.
    • The radial menu will automatically close itself if the tile it was opened from changes ownership.

title: Update 24.0
html:
OpenFront 24.0[1] was released July 18, 2025.

Major Changes

  • Stack units by building a unit of the same type on top
  • More ports => more gold per trade ship

⚖️ Balance Changes

  • Trade ships are now capped at 150 (Evan)
 → Each port you own now increases the gold per trade, counterbalancing the cap.
  • MIRVs have been nerfed
 → Expect less devastating multi-warhead nukes. Land in-between the fallout can be more quickly conquered.
  • Warships prioritize enemy transport ships over warships. Reload instantly after shooting a transport ship. (Evan)
  • Building discounts can only be used one time.

OpenFront 24.0 Open Beta was published on Github 27th of may.

Link to Github release


It contains an updated meta[1][2][3] and it changes how attacks work.

Commit 6b13522 - use newer attack, delete existing attack

"Also when a new attack is sent when there's an existing attack, have the new attack delete the existing attack. This causes attack to "reset" and use the entire border when a new attack is sent."[4]

Commit 9a17bc1 - counter attack doesn't cancel out attack

"Instead of a counter attack cancelling out the initial attack, both attacks run concurrently. This results in a more dynamic frontline."[5]

html:

📦 OpenFront v25.0 Changelog

⚙️ Major Changes

  • Removed workers & troop ratio bar

  • Trade ship spawn rate is determined by the number of ports players have and total number of trade ships on the map.

  • Ports and Factories share same price scaling

title: Update 33.0
html:
OpenFront v33 — Our biggest update yet: a new battle-royale gamemode, ranked 2v2, 22 new maps, impassable terrain, account usernames, custom tribe names and a major performance pass.

📦 OpenFront v33 Changelog

⭐ Major Changes

  • Doomsday Clock — A new battle-royale style zone gamemode. A shrinking doom zone drains troops (and warships) from doomed sides, with a 10-minute grace period and wave-based squeeze to break late-game stalemates. Now part of the public modifier rotation.
  • Ranked 2v2 — Ranked matchmaking now supports 2v2 alongside 1v1, with its own leaderboard ladder, clanmate pairing, and match cancellation for lobbies that don't fill or fully spawn.
  • Login with Google — Sign in with a Google account and link it to an existing account.
  • Account usernames + verified badge — Claim an account-level username (base.suffix, or a bare name for subscribers) and play under it with a verified badge next to your name.
  • Custom tribe names — Buy a custom tribe name in the store's new Tribes tab and it can appear on bot tribes in public games. Boosts make your tribe appear more often, and a public tribe leaderboard tracks how they do.
  • Impassable terrain — Mappers can now mark terrain as impassable, opening up a new class of map design. Several new maps already use it.
  • Warship veterancy — Warships gain veterancy over their service life.
  • MIRVs are real nukes now — MIRV warheads fly like standard nukes with per-type speeds and can be intercepted normally by SAMs. Launching a MIRV also puts the silo on cooldown.
  • Anonymous names — A lobby setting that replaces player names with memorable, collision-proof animal names.
  • 22 new maps — including Sol, Russia, United States, France, Germany, China, Vietnam, Scandinavia and the first maps built around impassable terrain.

title: Upgrading
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

Upgrading adds another completed level to a City, Factory, Port, Missile Silo, or SAM Launcher. Defense Posts cannot be upgraded.

Values by building

BuildingUpgrade build timeEffect of one completed levelUpgrade cost
City2 seconds+250,000 maximum troopsNext city-level price
Factory2 seconds+1 factory level for train-generation rollsNext shared port/factory-level price
Port5 seconds+1 trade-ship roll per second, +1 repair dock, +5 active repair HP/tickNext shared port/factory-level price
Missile Silo10 seconds+1 nuclear launch slot1,000,000
SAM Launcher30 seconds+1 missile slot and a larger range3,000,000 after the first launcher

Cost sequences

City levels cost min(1,000,000, 125,000 × 2owned city levels). Port and factory levels share min(1,000,000, 125,000 × 2owned port and factory levels). SAM ownership uses the count of launcher structures for price, so the first launcher costs 1,500,000 and later launcher builds or upgrades cost 3,000,000.

Cooldowns

A new Missile Silo or SAM level supplies another slot, but that slot begins its 90-tick (9-second) cooldown immediately and is not ready the instant construction completes.

Capture

When an upgraded building is captured, all completed levels transfer to the captor. The levels then count in the captor's capacity, slots, generation rolls, and future owned-level cost sequences.

title: Warship
html:
Gameplay values on this page were verified against OpenFront v0.33.1.

A Warship is a player-controlled naval unit that attacks transports and enemy warships, captures trade ships, gains veterancy, and repairs at ports.

Cost and movement

The cost is min(1,000,000, 250,000 × (owned warships + 1)). Warships normally move 1 tile per tick. While pursuing a trade ship they move 2 tiles per tick. A warship needs an owned Port to spawn.

Combat

  • Base health: 1,000.
  • Target range: 130 tiles.
  • Priority: transport ship, then warship, then trade ship.
  • Minimum interval between normal shots: 21 ticks, or 2.1 seconds. Transport targets bypass this reload check.
  • Shell speed: 3 tiles per tick.
  • Base damage roll: 200, 225, 250, 275, or 300 with equal probability.

A shell follows its target. If the firing warship is destroyed, its shell is removed after 50 further ticks (5 seconds).

Veterancy

LevelMaximum healthPossible shell damage
01,000200 / 225 / 250 / 275 / 300
11,200240 / 270 / 300 / 330 / 360
21,400280 / 315 / 350 / 385 / 420
31,600320 / 360 / 400 / 440 / 480

Veterancy is capped at level 3 and gives +20% of base maximum health and base damage per level. One enemy-warship killing blow grants a level and clears partial progress. Otherwise, 10 transport kills or 25 trade-ship captures grant a level; mixed progress shares a 250-point scale where a transport is worth 25 and a capture 10.

Repair

A warship passively heals 1 hit point per tick when within 150 Euclidean tiles of any owned port. Below 75% health it automatically seeks repair unless manually moved during the previous 50 ticks (5 seconds).

Docking requires a distance of 5 tiles. Each port level holds one warship and adds 5 hit points per tick to that port's active repair pool, split among docked ships, in addition to passive healing. A ship changes repair ports only when the new squared distance is less than 75% of the current squared distance. A player under the Doomsday penalty cannot heal or auto-retreat warships.

Trade-ship capture

The warship must have an active reachable home port, stay within a 100-tile patrol radius, and reach Manhattan distance 5. A trade ship is immune for its first 20 ticks after leaving shore. Captured ships return to the captor's nearest reachable active port.

title: World
html:
Not to be confused with Giant World Map or Known World.

Map of the World (sometimes referred to as the globe or Earth map) is a map that shows all of the 7 major continents of the world as well as all 5 major oceans of the world. This also included islands such as the Caribbean islands, the British isles, Iceland, New Zealand, Madagascar, Japan and others. However, smaller islands are not shown due to the size of the map.

The map's terrain is comprised of an even amount of flat, hilly and mountainous terrain that is quite evenly spread through the map. However, Asia tends to be more mountainous, Africa tends to be more hilly and South America tends to be more flat.

However, it should be noted that most of the map of water and with the Panama and Suez canals being a thing, this results in this being one of the best maps for trade ships and warships.

Nations

The map features 72 named nations, including United States, Canada, Mexico, Cuba, Colombia and Venezuela.
